researchUpdates.title: Iron Ore Tailings in Construction Materials: A Systematic Review of Composition and Water Absorption Performance
researchUpdates.authors: R. N. Silva and coauthors; complete names not independently verified from accessible publisher metadata
researchUpdates.summary: A systematic review maps how iron-ore tailings are used across construction materials, including geopolymer and alkali-activated matrices, with particular attention to composition and water absorption.
highlights: The review separates tailings used as aggregate, filler, raw material or supplementary cementitious material instead of treating every incorporation route as equivalent.
Cross-study water-absorption comparisons are limited by varied matrices, test ages, production methods and incomplete reporting of statistical variability.
researchUpdates.access: Review-level synthesis, not independent experimental replication. The detailed water-absorption subset is modest and heterogeneous, some ages are missing, and tailings chemistry and potentially toxic elements require source-specific assessment.
researchUpdates.summaryBasis: Primary publisher article page and metadata; cited studies and supplements not individually audited

journalArticle.title: Tailings content is not a material identity
journalArticle.summary: A new systematic review shows why tailings role, chemistry and test conditions must accompany any replacement percentage.
paragraphs: Iron-ore tailings appear as aggregate, filler, precursor-like raw material and supplementary cementitious material across different matrices. A single percentage cannot describe those distinct functions.

For the formulation database, tailings records should preserve mineralogy, particle size, processing, functional role, matrix, curing and water-absorption age. This review organizes prior evidence; it does not validate a universal tailings recipe or independently reproduce the underlying experiments.
